title: Solomaxxing Date-Cost Simulator
oneLiner: Single Gen Z users turn dating-app fatigue and expensive dates into intentional solo plans they can actually feel proud of.
theme: 외로움 / 역전 / 자산 방어 - making singlehood feel intentional instead of failed.
targetUser: Gen Z singles, recently broken-up adults, and friend groups reframing solo time as a status-positive lifestyle choice.
keyUX: User compares date cost, emotional recovery, hobby goals, social pressure, and weekend energy; the app builds a solomaxxing itinerary, savings flex, and shareable solo-progress card.
requiredUISections: Solo status header with date-cost savings and energy budget
Dating pressure vs personal-goal tradeoff sliders
Weekend itinerary builder for hobby, rest, fitness, culture, and friend touchpoints
Spend comparison for date night vs solo upgrade
Confidence ritual and no-settling pledge cards
sourceSignals: S14 - Wired, solomaxxing among Gen Z singles links dating costs, app fatigue, and intentional singlehood as a lifestyle signal: https://www.wired.com/story/solomaxxing
stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Solomaxxing Date-Cost Simulator" for Gen Z singles turning expensive dating fatigue into intentional solo plans. The first screen must be a working simulator with a solo status header, dating pressure vs personal-goal sliders, weekend itinerary builder, date-night vs solo-upgrade spend comparison, confidence ritual cards, no-settling pledge, social-pressure response script, and shareable progress poster. Use realistic sample data: $189 average date cost, three dating-app matches ignored, pottery class, gym block, solo dinner, friend voice note, $72 saved this weekend, and a post-breakup confidence goal. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with a bold shareable first impression, strong but controlled accent color, crisp hierarchy, and a poster-like output that still leaves the main workflow obvious. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
